**Install as an app** (`notifications.install-instructions`) ✅

- A collapsible "Install Ember as a web app." sits on your profile and in the notification setup help, and is hidden inside the installed app.
- Browsers the user agent reports as Chrome (Chrome, Chromium Edge, Brave, Chrome on iPhone and iPad) and Firefox on a computer don't get it at all.
- EdgeHTML gets "Click [the app available - install Ember chat button] in the address bar." and "Click Install."; Firefox on Android gets "Tap the [More options] menu button." and "Tap Install in the menu."
- Safari on a Mac, as iPadOS Safari reports itself, gets "Click File in the top left." and "Click Add to Dock…."; Safari on iPhone and iPad gets "To receive push notifications in Safari for &lt;iPhone or iPad&gt;, you must install Ember as a web app.", "Tap [the share button]" and "Tap Add to Home Screen."
- Anything else gets "Some platforms require you to install Ember as a web app to receive push notifications."
- Install now appears only after the browser offers to install the app, opens the browser's install prompt, and hides once the app is installed.

Note: Install now is the ink button wherever it shows, where ember-rust's header styles leave the dialog's clear, its icon white on white, and it goes once pressed, since a browser prompts only once for each offer, where Campfire's stays and does nothing. Edge's step keeps its button apart from the next word, which ember-rust runs together. ember-rust's steps for Chrome on Android never show, since Chrome gets no install steps, so they aren't ported. Install now takes the place of the browser's own offer only in the browsers given the steps, as Campfire's controller does, but on every page once `/api/bootstrap` has said which browser this is, where the controller does on the pages that show the steps (every room's and your profile); an offer that comes before then is kept for Install now and left to the browser too.

When only one is visible, it opens by itself.

- Safari on a Mac gets "Click Safari in the top left.", "Click Settings….", "Click the Websites tab.", "Click Notifications in the sidebar.", "Click &lt;site address&gt; in the list." and "Select Allow."; Firefox and Chrome on Android get their own steps; any other browser gets "Ensure notifications are enabled for &lt;site address&gt; in your web browser settings."

- Platforms are read as the `useragent` gem reads them: Chromium Edge, Brave and Chrome on iPhone and iPad count as Chrome, Firefox and Edge on iPhone and iPad as Safari, and iPadOS Safari, which reports a Mac, as Safari on a Mac.

Note: The Worker reads the platform from the user agent as ember-rust does, checked against Rails' answers for ember-rust's 385 user agents, and gives it to the app with `/api/bootstrap` (`platform`). The help is checked against ember-rust's goldens of its partials for ten browsers (`apps/web/src/components/workspace/golden/`). The Apple menu's logo is named as a picture (`role="img"`), since screen readers don't read the label ember-rust gives its `em`. Desktops other than Windows and macOS, such as Linux and ChromeOS, get ember-rust's sentence for a system it has no steps for ("Ensure notifications are allowed for &lt;browser&gt; in your system settings.") where ember-rust gives them macOS's steps.

**Web Push configuration** (`notifications.web-push-keys`) ✅

- `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` and `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`, a P-256 key pair in URL-safe Base64, turn Web Push on. Without them (a blank value counts as unset) push is off, and "Web Push is off: VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY and VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY aren't set" is logged.
- A pair that doesn't parse or doesn't match also turns push off, logging "Web Push is off: " followed by "VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY isn't a Base64 P-256 public key", "VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY isn't a Base64 P-256 private key" or "VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY isn't the public key of VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY".
- With push off, nothing is pushed, pages carry no public key, the bell explains "Notifications aren’t configured", and test pushes fail.
- Each push carries a VAPID token signed with the key pair (ES256, valid for 12 hours) whose contact is `VAPID_SUBJECT`, by default `https://` and the deployment's domain, or the project's own URL when it has none.

Note: The keys are Worker secrets, read once per isolate. The app gets the public key from `/api/bootstrap` (`vapidPublicKey`), where ember-rust puts it in a meta tag, and always uncompressed, which is what browsers subscribe with, where ember-rust passes on a compressed key as it's given. `/api/health` says whether push is on and why not (`push`), which ember-rust only logs, without failing the check. `pnpm vapid:keys` prints a new pair, and the preview's first deploy makes one (`platform.deploy-secrets`). Pushes are signed with the pair (`notifications.push`). Without `VAPID_SUBJECT` they name this project's URL, as ember-rust's do without `TLS_DOMAIN`, since a Worker has no setting for its domain. Your browsers' subscriptions can each be sent a test push from `/users/me/push_subscriptions` (`notifications.test-page`).

- Administrators open `/account/bots` (titled "Chat bots") from the "Chat bots" button in Workspace settings, and its back link returns there. Members get 403.
- The page shows "Chat bots" and "With Chat bots, other sites and services can post updates directly to Ember." with a translation globe, and "Add a chat bot", which opens `/account/bots/new`.
- Active bots are listed by name, ignoring case, each with its avatar (linking to its profile), its name and an edit link ("Edit &lt;name&gt;" to screen readers). With no bots the list is simply empty.
- Under each bot, every room it's in (open or private, not DMs, by name ignoring case) offers two read-only commands: `curl -d 'Hello!' <url>` ("curl command for posting messages") and `curl -F "attachment=@/path/to/file" <url>` ("curl command for posting attachments").
- `<url>` is absolute, on the host the page was requested from: `<origin>/rooms/<room id>/<bot key>/messages`.
- "Copy message command" and "Copy attachment command" copy their line to the clipboard and flash the button for a second; if the clipboard refuses, nothing shows.

Note: Administrators open `/account/bots` from the Chat bots button at the top of workspace settings, whose label, like Custom styles', is hidden at 500px wide and below. It lists the active bots from `GET /api/account/bots`, by name ignoring case, as the people directory lists people, each with its avatar linking to its page, its name, a link to its settings and, for each room it's in but its DMs, by name ignoring case, the two curl commands for posting to the room as it, at `<origin>/rooms/<room id>/<bot key>/messages` on the host the page was loaded from, with buttons that copy them and play their success animation. A bot deleted or renamed elsewhere, as by another administrator, leaves the list or takes its new name, and its place by it, as soon as the workspace socket says so, where ember-rust's keeps it as it was until the page loads again. Keys are answered with `Cache-Control: no-store`, as secrets no cache should keep. Anyone else who opens the page is sent to workspace settings with the alert "Only administrators can manage bots", where ember-rust answers an empty 403 page, as Custom styles does (`accounts.custom-css`). The translation globe sits beside the heading, where ember-rust's sits at the panel's corner over the heading's first letters. Both commands post through the bot API (`bots.api-post`).

**Add and edit a bot** (`bots.create-edit`) ✅

- `/account/bots/new` ("New chat bot") and `/account/bots/<id>/edit` ("Edit bot") show "Chat bot setup" and "Connect a bot to your workspace and choose where updates are delivered." above the bot form, and link back to the bots page.
- The form has an avatar picker ("Upload bot avatar", images only), Bot name (placeholder "Name the bot", required, autofocused) and Webhook URL (placeholder "Webhook URL", a URL field), each label with a translation globe, and Save changes.
- A chosen picture previews at once ("Bot avatar"); without one the default bot picture shows, and an avatar can't be removed.
- Saving returns to the bots page with no confirmation message. A new bot gets a token of 12 random letters and digits and joins every open room, like a new person.
- Only the browser checks the fields: the server saves whatever webhook text and name it gets, even an empty name.
- Creating a bot with Webhook URL left empty still saves an empty webhook, whose deliveries fail without a reply. When editing, a blank URL removes the webhook, and a filled one adds or changes it.
- Unknown or deleted bots are 404, and members get 403.

Note: Add a chat bot (`/account/bots/new`) and a bot's settings (`/account/bots/<id>/edit`) show ember-rust's form, and Save changes goes back to the bots page with no notice. The form posts JSON `{name, webhookUrl}` to `POST /api/account/bots`, which answers 201 with the bot, and a bot's settings load with `GET /api/account/bots/<id>` and save with `PATCH`, which is sent only the fields changed, where ember-rust's form always sends both, so a save doesn't put back what another administrator saved since. With a picture chosen in Upload bot avatar, which previews at once in place of the bot's avatar, or of Campfire's default bot picture for a new bot, the form goes as a multipart form instead, its `user` part the JSON and its `avatar` and `variant` parts the picture and the variant the browser makes of it, as the profile's photo does (`users.avatar-upload`), with its 16 MB limit; a save without one keeps the avatar, which, as in ember-rust, can be replaced but not removed. A new bot gets a token of 12 random letters and digits and joins every open room. Unlike ember-rust, a name must have more than spaces (422 "Name can't be blank"), and a webhook URL is trimmed and must be an http or https URL with a host, at most 2,048 characters (422 "Webhook URL must be an http or https URL"), each said in the workspace's alert with what was typed kept; a bot has a webhook only while it has somewhere to deliver, so adding one without a URL saves none, and a blank URL removes it. A new name or avatar reaches every page signed in at once (`user.updated`), never with the key, and R2 deletes the avatar replaced. Signed in as an administrator, the settings of anyone but an active bot answer Campfire's 404 page, as ember-rust's do. Anyone else is sent to workspace settings with an alert (`bots.list`), from Add a chat bot before it shows. A bot's name is kept to 100 characters, as a person's is (`auth.first-run`), where ember-rust saves any.

**Delete a bot** (`bots.delete`) ✅

- The edit page's red "Delete bot" button ("Delete this chat bot") asks "Are you sure you want to permanently remove this bot from the account? This can’t be undone." and then returns to the bots page.
- Deleting deactivates the bot: it leaves the bots page and every room but its DMs, and its key stops working at once.
- Its messages and boosts stay, and its page reads "&lt;name&gt; is no longer on this account".
- Its token and webhook are kept, so deliveries already queued still go out and their replies still post.
- Members get 403, and unknown or already deleted bots 404.

Note: The bot's settings end with Delete bot, which asks ember-rust's question in the browser's own dialog, then sends `DELETE /api/account/bots/<id>`, answered 204, and goes back to the bots page. The bot is deactivated as someone removed is (`accounts.remove-person`): it leaves the bots page and every room but its DMs, every open page hears so (`user.updated`), and its page says it's no longer on this account (`users.show`). Its token and webhook are kept. Its key stops working in the bot API at once (`bots.api-auth`). Deliveries already on their way to it still go (`bots.webhook-jobs`), and what it says back still posts (`bots.webhook-reply`).

**Bot keys** (`bots.api-auth`) ✅

- Bots call `/rooms/<room id>/<bot key>/messages` and the paths under it, optionally ending in `.json`. The key is `<bot id>-<token>`: surrounding spaces are ignored, as is anything after a second `-`, and only active bots match.
- A key with an empty token matches nothing, so `<person id>-` can't post or edit as that person.
- A wrong key answers 302 to `/session/new` and changes nothing. A room the bot isn't in is an empty 404.
- Requests authenticated by a key skip forgery protection. A request carrying a session cookie acts as that person instead, with the usual checks.
- A valid key sent to any other page that needs signing in (as a `bot_key` parameter) gets an empty 403.
- Writes from banned IP addresses get 429.

Note: Bots call `/rooms/<room id>/<bot key>/messages` and the addresses of its messages and boosts under it, each with or without `.json`, which the Worker answers before any page. The key is read as ember-rust reads it (`User.authenticate_bot`): spaces around it are dropped, as JavaScript trims them, the bot's id is what comes before its first `-` and its token what comes between that and the next, and the token must be the active bot's current one, compared in constant time, so a key with an empty token matches nothing and a deleted bot's key or a replaced one stops working at once. A room the bot isn't in, or that doesn't exist, is an empty 404, and its object is never woken. Posts, edits, deletions and boosts from banned IP addresses get 429, as other writes do (`users.ban`). Unlike ember-rust, a key that names no active bot answers 401 `{"error":"Unknown bot key"}`, where ember-rust redirects a script to sign in. These addresses never read a session cookie, so a request carrying one still acts as the bot, where ember-rust acts as the cookie's person, and nothing but the key in the address makes a request anyone's, so posts from other sites are taken without a forgery check. No other address reads a bot key, so a request with only one answers 401 there, where ember-rust answers 403.

**Bots post messages** (`bots.api-post`) ✅

- POSTing to a room's bot URL posts the raw request body, whatever its Content-Type, as the bot's message: `curl -d 'Hello!'` posts "Hello!" and a JSON body posts its JSON text. UTF-8 is kept, emoji included; ember-rust replaces invalid bytes with U+FFFD.
- The body is rich text: HTML renders, and mention attachments mention people and reach mentioned bots' webhooks.
- It answers 201 with an empty body and `Location: <origin>/messages/<id>`, a URL that answers 404 because it names no room.
- A multipart `attachment` posts a file message instead, processed like an upload, whose text for search, push and webhooks is the file name.
- A blank body (empty or only whitespace) with no file is 422, as is a multipart body without `attachment` in ember-rust, and a room the bot isn't in is 404; none of them posts anything.
- A text body over 16 MiB, or a file over 250,000,000 bytes, gets 413.
- The message reaches the room like anyone's (live, unread, pushed, searchable) and triggers other bots' webhooks, never the sender's own, even when it mentions itself or is in its own DM.

Note: POSTing to a room's address for bots posts the request's body, whatever its type, as the bot's message, as rich text, read as UTF-8 with invalid bytes replaced. It answers 201 with an empty body and `Location` set to the message's permalink, `<origin>/rooms/<room id>/@<id>`, on the host it was asked at, where ember-rust's `/messages/<id>` answers 404. The message reaches the room as anyone's does: live, unread, pushed and searchable, and is delivered to the webhooks of the other bots it's for, never its sender's (`bots.webhook-delivery`). A body that's empty or only spaces is an empty 422. Unlike ember-rust, which takes up to 16 MiB of anything, more than 100,000 characters of markup is 413 `{"status":413,"error":"Content Too Large"}`, more than 10,000 characters of text is 422 `{"error":"Messages can be up to 10,000 characters."}`, as the composer allows, and markup that shows nothing, such as `<p> </p>`, is 422 `{"error":"Your message is empty."}` rather than an empty message. A form, as `curl -F 'attachment=@report.pdf'` sends one, posts its `attachment` as the bot's file message, as a browser's upload is posted (`attachments.upload`): typed by its bytes, then the type the form gives it, then its name, shown as a file sent without a preview is (`attachments.previews`), and found by search, pushed and delivered to webhooks by its name. R2 keeps the file as it arrives, a part at a time, so the Worker never holds more than a part of it (apps/worker/src/files/form-parts.ts and streamed.ts), and the key is checked again once all of it has arrived, as it is for text. A form without `attachment`, or whose `attachment` is empty, is an empty 422, as in ember-rust. Unlike ember-rust, which keeps the last `attachment` a form sends, as Rack does, the first one counts, but for file fields left empty, which Rack leaves out too; `attachment` sent as text is 422 `{"error":"An attachment has to be a file"}`, where ember-rust answers 500; a form that can't be read is 400 `{"status":400,"error":"Bad Request"}`, as is a body typed `multipart/form-data` that names no boundary to read it by, as when its sender sets the type itself, which ember-rust posts as text, its parts' headers and bytes and all; a file over 250,000,000 bytes is 413 `{"status":413,"error":"Content Too Large"}` as soon as that much of it has arrived; a name longer than 255 characters is 422 `{"error":"That file's name can't be kept"}`; and without an R2 bucket a form is 503 `{"error":"Ember isn't set up to store files"}`, as a browser's upload is.

**Bots read messages** (`bots.api-list`) ✅

- GET on a room's bot URL answers `application/json; charset=utf-8` with its newest 40 messages, oldest first; `?before=<id>` gives the 40 created before that message and `?after=<id>` the 40 after it, and `before` wins when both are given. An empty room gives `[]`.
- Each message has, in order, `id`, `created_at` (UTC ISO 8601 with milliseconds), `body` (`plain_text`, `html`), `creator` (`id`, `name`, `role`, `avatar_url`), `room` (`id`) and `url`. `role` is "member", "administrator" or "bot".
- `html` is the rendered rich text inside `<div class="lexxy-content">`. A file message has its file name as `plain_text`, `""` as `html` and no file URL.
- `<`, `>` and `&` are escaped as `\u003c`, `\u003e` and `\u0026`; emoji are written as they are.
- `avatar_url` and `url` (`<origin>/rooms/<room id>/messages/<id>`) are absolute, built from each request's host; a forged `X-Forwarded-Host` never shows up in another request's response.
- `X-Total-Count` gives the room's message count on every page ("0" when empty). `Link: <<origin>/rooms/<room id>/<bot key>/messages?before=<first id>>; rel="next"` appears only when older messages exist, or with `?after` as `?after=<last id>` when newer ones do.
- A cursor that isn't a message in this room is 404 `{"status":404,"error":"Not Found"}`. HEAD gives the same headers without a body.

Note: GET or HEAD on a room's address for bots answers its messages as ember-rust's `index` does: the newest 40, oldest first, or the 40 before `?before` or after `?after`, `before` winning when both are given, when the `Link` still follows the page's last message, and a blank cursor being none. Answers are `application/json; charset=utf-8`, with `<`, `>` and `&` escaped as Rails escapes them, `X-Total-Count` and, while there's a next page, a `Link` to it, and every address on the host the request came to. A cursor that isn't one of the room's messages is 404 `{"status":404,"error":"Not Found"}`. As Rack::ETag gives them, answers carry an ETag and `Cache-Control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate`, and a copy that's current gets 304. Each message is `messages/_message.json`'s, with its writer's name, role and avatar as they are now. Unlike ember-rust, ids are strings, as all of Ember's are; `url` is the message's permalink, `<origin>/rooms/<room id>/@<id>`, which opens its room at it, where ember-rust's is `/rooms/<room id>/messages/<id>`; and `html` has mentions and link previews as they're stored, without the avatar and name ember-rust renders inside a mention. A file message's `plain_text` is its file's name and its `html` empty, as ember-rust writes a message without rich text.

**Bots edit and delete their messages** (`bots.api-edit-delete`) ✅

- PUT or PATCH on `…/messages/<id>` replaces the bot's own message with the raw body and answers 200 with the message's JSON, shaped as in the list. The body isn't checked for blank, so an empty one empties the message.
- A multipart `attachment` replaces the message's file and keeps its text, and an empty `attachment=` field removes the file.
- DELETE removes the bot's own message and its boosts and answers 204.
- Someone else's message is an empty 403, a message outside the room is 404 `{"status":404,"error":"Not Found"}`, and a room the bot isn't in is an empty 404. None of them changes anything.
- Edits and deletions reach the room live, and edits never trigger webhooks.

Note: PUT or PATCH on a message's address for bots, `/rooms/<room id>/<bot key>/messages/<id>`, replaces the text of the bot's own message with the request's body, as rich text, as a socket's edit does: the message is marked edited, and text saved as it was leaves it as it was. It answers 200 with the message as the list writes it, with its ETag. DELETE deletes the message and its boosts and answers 204. Both reach the room live, and search finds the message as it is now. Someone else's message is an empty 403, a message outside the room is 404 `{"status":404,"error":"Not Found"}`, and a room the bot isn't in is an empty 404; none of them changes anything. Unlike ember-rust, which saves any body, an empty one included, text is held to what the edit form allows, as a post's is (`bots.api-post`): text that shows nothing is 422 `{"error":"Your message is empty."}`, more than 10,000 characters of it 422 `{"error":"Messages can be up to 10,000 characters."}`, and more than 100,000 characters of markup 413. A form's `attachment` file replaces the message's file, or gives a message of text one, which it shows in place of its text, keeping the text, as ember-rust's `update` does, R2 keeping it as a post's file is (`bots.api-post`); an `attachment` with nothing in it takes the file away, and leaves a message without one as it was. Either way the message is marked edited, as an edit of its text is, and R2 deletes the file it had (`attachments.purge`). Unlike ember-rust, a form without `attachment`, which ember-rust reads as an empty body that empties the message's text, is an empty 422, and `attachment` sent as text, which ember-rust answers 500, is 422 `{"error":"An attachment has to be a file"}`; neither changes anything. A form that can't be read, or a body typed `multipart/form-data` that names no boundary, is 400, as a post's is, where ember-rust saves a body without a boundary as the message's text.

**Bots boost messages** (`bots.api-boosts`) ✅

- POSTing to `…/messages/<id>/boosts` boosts the message with the raw body as its content, untrimmed and of any length, and answers 201 with the boost's JSON. A bot may boost any message in the room, its own included, and add the same boost again.
- Boost JSON has, in order, `id`, `content`, `created_at`, `booster` (`id`, `name`, `role`, `avatar_url`) and `message` (`id`, `url`).
- A room the bot isn't in, or a message outside the room, is an empty 404, checked before a blank body's 422.
- DELETE on `…/boosts/<boost id>` removes the bot's own boost on that message with 204; anyone else's, or one already removed, is an empty 404.
- New and removed boosts reach the room live.

Note: POSTing to a message's boosts address for bots, `/rooms/<room id>/<bot key>/messages/<id>/boosts`, boosts it with the request's body and answers 201 with the boost's JSON, in Campfire's order of keys, with its ETag. A bot may boost any message in the room, its own included, and add the same boost again, which the room shows as another reaction, where a person's repeated click adds nothing. DELETE on `…/boosts/<boost id>` removes the bot's own boost on that message with 204. Both reach the room live. A message outside the room, or a room the bot isn't in, is an empty 404, checked before a blank body's empty 422; anyone else's boost, the bot's own under another message, or one already removed is an empty 404. Unlike ember-rust, which keeps the body as it comes, a boost is trimmed and holds at most 16 characters, as a person's does: ember-rust's column is `varchar(16)`, which SQLite doesn't enforce. A longer one is 422 `{"error":"Boosts can be up to 16 characters."}`.

**Webhooks** (`bots.webhook-delivery`) ✅

- Creating a message, in the app or through the bot API, notifies bots: in a DM, every active bot in it; elsewhere, every active bot it mentions who is a member of the room. The sender and bots without a webhook are skipped, each bot gets one delivery, and a typed "@Name" that isn't a real mention doesn't count.
- Edits, boosts and webhook replies never trigger deliveries.
- The POST is JSON with, in order, `user` (`id`, `name`: the sender), `room` (`id`, `name`, `path`) and `message` (`id`, `body` with `html` and `plain`, `path`). `room.name` is null in a DM, `room.path` is the receiving bot's own `/rooms/<room id>/<bot key>/messages`, and `message.path` is `/rooms/<room id>/@<message id>`.
- `html` is the stored rich text without its layout, and `plain` the plain text with every `@<bot name>` of the receiving bot removed and surrounding Unicode whitespace trimmed. A file message has a null `html` and its file name as `plain`, and never a file URL.
- Requests send `Content-Type: application/json`, `Accept: */*` and `User-Agent: Ruby`, accept gzip and deflate, and escape `<`, `>` and `&` in the JSON as `\u003c`, `\u003e` and `\u0026`.
- Any http or https URL and port is accepted, redirects aren't followed and nothing is retried. An invalid URL, such as the empty one a bot created without a URL has, fails without a reply.
- Webhooks may point at internal hosts: there's no private-network guard, since only administrators set them.

Note: A new message, from the composer or the bot API, is delivered once the Workspace applies it from its room's log, which it does once however often the room sends it: to the webhooks of the active bots it mentions that are in its room, or in a DM to those of every active bot in it, never to its author, and to each once. Edits and boosts deliver nothing. Each delivery POSTs Campfire's JSON, in its order of keys and with `<`, `>` and `&` escaped, to the URL as it was saved: `html` is the message's stored rich text and `plain` its plain text without the receiving bot's @mentions. It sends Net::HTTP's `Content-Type`, `Accept` and `User-Agent`, but leaves `Accept-Encoding` to the Worker's `fetch`, which sends none in local development, and Cloudflare adds `CF-Worker`, naming the Worker's host. Redirects aren't followed and nothing is retried. Unlike Campfire, a webhook's URL is checked when it's saved (`bots.create-edit`), and a bot without one has no webhook, so nothing is tried for it, where Campfire tries the empty URL and fails. Nothing guards where a webhook points, but a deployed Worker reaches the internet, not a private network, so a webhook on one needs a public address, such as a Cloudflare Tunnel's. What a bot says back is delivered to no webhook (`bots.webhook-reply`). A file message's `html` is null and its `plain` its file's name, as Campfire delivers a message without rich text.

**Webhook replies** (`bots.webhook-reply`) ✅

- A reply with status exactly 200 and media type exactly `text/plain` or `text/html` (parameters ignored, case-sensitive) is posted by the bot as a rich-text message in the message's room, even if the bot has left it. An empty one posts an empty message, and ember-rust replaces invalid UTF-8.
- Any other reply with a Content-Type, whatever its status, becomes a file message processed like an upload: a 500 `text/html` page is `attachment.html` and a 201 `text/plain` reply `attachment.text`. Redirects aren't followed, so a 3xx with a type becomes a file too.
- File names and types come from Rails' MIME table: `image/jpeg` gives `attachment.jpeg`, `audio/mp4` gives `attachment.m4a` typed `audio/aac`, and unregistered types such as `application/x-foo` or `Text/Plain` give `attachment.` typed as sent.
- Nothing is posted when the reply has no Content-Type, an empty one or one without `/`, or when the connection is refused or fails on DNS or TLS. gzip and deflate replies are decoded first.
- If connecting or reading takes over 7 seconds, the bot posts "Failed to respond within 7 seconds". ember-rust also gives up after 60 seconds in all ("Failed to respond within 60 seconds") and posts nothing for replies over 100 MiB.
- Replies reach the room like other messages (live, unread, pushed) but never trigger further webhooks.

Note: A delivery reads the webhook's answer as Campfire's `Webhook#deliver` does, replaying the answers ember-rust recorded from it: a 200 whose media type is exactly `text/plain` or `text/html` is text, any other answer with a Content-Type is a file, named and typed by Rails' MIME table, an answer without one says nothing, and one whose type isn't a media type fails the delivery. The text is posted as the bot's message, as rich text, as a bot's post is, even once the bot has left the room or been deleted: live, marking the room unread and pushed as any new message is, but delivered to no webhook. A webhook that doesn't answer, or send the next part of its answer, within 7 seconds, or finish within 60, as ember-rust's deadline has it, has the bot say "Failed to respond within 7 seconds" (or 60). The Worker's `fetch` decodes a gzipped answer. Unlike Campfire, a reply with nothing in it, or too long for a message, isn't posted, as no message is, and its delivery is logged as failed. Invalid UTF-8 is replaced, as ember-rust replaces it, and no more of a text reply is read than a message's markup can take, where ember-rust reads up to 100 MB of any answer. A file is posted as the bot's file message, `attachment.<extension>`, typed and shown as a file a bot posts is (`bots.api-post`), R2 keeping it as it arrives, a part at a time, where Campfire reads all of it first; only the time spent waiting on the webhook counts toward its 7 seconds, not the time R2 takes. A file larger than 100 MiB fails the delivery, logged as "the reply is larger than 100 MB" as ember-rust logs it, and posts nothing, as does one whose room is deleted while it arrives, which R2 then deletes. Without an R2 bucket, a file reply fails the delivery, logged with its name and type.

**Where bots show up** (`bots.membership`) ✅

- A new bot joins every open room at the `mentions` level, and rooms made open later add it too; deleting a bot takes it out of every room but its DMs.
- Private rooms' member pickers list active bots with everyone else, and anyone can start a DM with an active bot.
- Bots are offered in @-mention suggestions for rooms they're in, and in the DM picker's search and suggested people.
- Bots never appear in Workspace settings' people list and never get the administrator crown.

Note: A bot is a member as anyone active is. Adding one puts it in every open room at `mentions` (`bots.create-edit`), and a new open room, or a private one made open, takes in every active bot with everyone else (`rooms.open`). The New room forms and a room's settings list active bots among everyone, by name (`rooms.members`), anyone can start a DM with one (`dms.create`), the composer offers a room's active bots to mention (`mentions.autocomplete`), and New direct message's search finds them and the sidebar suggests them (`dms.picker`, `dms.suggestions`). Workspace settings' people list leaves bots out, so they get no crown, and the server refuses to change a bot's role (`accounts.roles`). Deleting a bot takes it out of every room but its DMs (`bots.delete`), and out of every picker and suggestion.

**A bot's profile** (`bots.profile`) ✅

- `/users/<bot id>` shows the bot's avatar ("Profile avatar", the default bot picture without an upload) and, while the bot is active, a button that starts a DM with it. There's no name heading, bio, email, sign-in link or ban button, even for administrators.
- A deleted bot's page shows only its avatar and "&lt;name&gt; is no longer on this account".

Note: `GET /api/users/<bot id>` answers a bot as the people directory lists it, with no sign-in link even for administrators (`users.show`), and its avatar is Campfire's default-bot-avatar.svg, byte for byte (`users.avatars`). The page shows that avatar and, while the bot is active, ember-rust's `button_to_direct_room_with`: Campfire's plain full-width button with the messages icon, "Ping &lt;name&gt;" to screen readers, which starts a DM with the bot or opens the one you have, as a person's does. Its `btn--primary` and `txt--large`, and the classes on the `div` around it, are ones Campfire doesn't define, so it's drawn without them. The avatars on the bots page link here (`users.avatar-links`).

Sources: [`crates/views/templates/users/show.html`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/views/templates/users/show.html) · [`reference/app/views/users/show.html.erb`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/app/views/users/show.html.erb) · [`crates/views/src/helpers/users.rs`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/views/src/helpers/users.rs) · [`crates/ember/src/controllers/users/avatars.rs`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/ember/src/controllers/users/avatars.rs) · [`reference/app/controllers/users/avatars_controller.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/app/controllers/users/avatars_controller.rb)

ember-rust tests: [`parity/screens.yml`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/parity/screens.yml)

**Bot keys in logs** (`bots.log-redaction`) ✅

- Campfire's Rails log shows the key in every bot URL on a line as `[FILTERED]` (`/rooms/1/[FILTERED]/messages`, also inside a logged `Link` header) and filters a `bot_key` parameter, leaving other room paths alone.
- ember-rust's request log, which follows Thruster's, records each request's path and query in full, bot keys included, unless `LOG_REQUESTS` turns it off.

Note: When a request fails, the Worker's log line names its address with any bot key in it `[FILTERED]`, as Campfire's `LogScrubbingFormatter` filters it (`/rooms/<room id>/[FILTERED]/messages`), and a bot's request answers 500 `{"status":500,"error":"Internal Server Error"}`. Like ember-rust's request log, Cloudflare's own record of each request (Workers Logs and traces) keeps its whole URL, keys included, so whoever can read those logs can read keys.

Sources: [`reference/lib/rails_ext/log_scrubbing_formatter.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/lib/rails_ext/log_scrubbing_formatter.rb) · [`reference/config/initializers/filter_parameter_logging.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/config/initializers/filter_parameter_logging.rb) · [`reference/config/environments/production.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/config/environments/production.rb) · [`crates/kit/src/front/handler.rs`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/kit/src/front/handler.rs)

ember-rust tests: [`reference/test/lib/rails_ext/log_scrubbing_formatter_test.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/test/lib/rails_ext/log_scrubbing_formatter_test.rb)

**Webhooks run in the background** (`bots.webhook-jobs`) ✅

- Deliveries are queued once the message is saved and run in the background on their own queue, so a slow webhook never holds up the message's request, pushes or other jobs.
- `JOB_CONCURRENCY` deliveries (2 by default) run at a time and up to 1,024 more wait; beyond that a delivery is dropped and logged as "job queue is full, dropping job".
- Nothing is retried. The bot, message and webhook are read when the delivery runs: a message deleted or a webhook removed by then fails it with nothing sent, an edit made by then is delivered, and a bot deleted by then still gets it.
- Each delivery logs "performed", or "job failed" with its cause.
- On shutdown, queued deliveries still run for up to 10 seconds; a crash loses them.

Note: A room delivers its new messages in the background once the Workspace has applied them, so neither a message's request nor its pushes wait on a webhook. As ember-rust's job runner does, 2 deliveries run at a time and up to 1,024 more wait their turn, but each room has its own queue, so one room's slow webhooks never hold up another's. Beyond that a delivery is dropped and logged as `dropped: the room's webhook queue is full`. Nothing is retried. The message is read when its turn comes, so an edit made by then is delivered and a message deleted by then fails with nothing sent. Unlike ember-rust, which reads the bot and its webhook then too, they're as they were when the Workspace applied the message: a bot deleted since still gets it, as in ember-rust, but so does a webhook removed since, and a delivery waiting when the bot's key is reset carries the old key. Each delivery logs `Bot::WebhookJob of message <id> to bot <id> performed:` with the webhook's status, or `no answer in time`, once what the bot says back is posted (`bots.webhook-reply`), or `failed:` with its reason, never with the webhook's URL or the bot's key. A deploy resets every room's object, which ends the deliveries waiting or running in it, as a crash ends ember-rust's.

Sources: [`crates/ember/src/jobs.rs`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/ember/src/jobs.rs) · [`crates/ember/src/integrations/jobs.rs`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/ember/src/integrations/jobs.rs) · [`crates/ember/src/config.rs`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/ember/src/config.rs) · [`crates/ember/src/app.rs`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/ember/src/app.rs) · [`reference/app/jobs/bot/webhook_job.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/app/jobs/bot/webhook_job.rb) · [`reference/app/jobs/application_job.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/app/jobs/application_job.rb)

ember-rust tests: [`crates/ember/src/jobs/tests.rs`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/ember/src/jobs/tests.rs)

**Slack-compatible webhooks** (`bots.slack-webhook`) ✅

- `POST /rooms/<room id>/<bot key>/slack` posts what a Slack incoming webhook is sent as the bot's message: JSON, whatever the request's type says, or a form's `payload` field, urlencoded or multipart.
- It answers as Slack's webhooks do, as text: 200 `ok`; 400 `invalid_payload` for no JSON object, `no_text` for nothing to show, `too_many_attachments` past 100 and `msg_too_long` past a message's 10,000 characters; 403 `invalid_token` for a key that isn't an active bot's; 404 `channel_not_found` for a room the bot isn't in; and 413 `msg_too_long` for a body past 100,000 characters.
- `text` is mrkdwn: *bold*, _italics_, ~strike-through~, `code`, code blocks between triple backticks, `>` and `>>>` quotes, `<url|label>` links to web and email addresses, emoji by name with skin tones, and the escapes `&amp;`, `&lt;` and `&gt;`. Formatting needs a word's edge, so `node_cpu_seconds_total` keeps its underscores, and `mrkdwn: false` leaves only links, mentions, emoji and escapes.
- Mentions, `<@U…>`, `<#C…|name>`, `<!subteam^…|@handle>`, `<!here>`, `<!channel>` and `<!everyone>`, show as text and notify nobody, and `<!date^…|fallback>` shows its fallback.
- `blocks` show in place of `text`, which shows when they show nothing. Header, section, context, Markdown, rich text and actions blocks post as rich text, and legacy `attachments` as quotes after their pretext, with their blocks inside, formatted only in the fields their `mrkdwn_in` names, or as their fallback when nothing else in them shows.
- `username`, `icon_emoji`, `icon_url`, `channel` and `thread_ts` change nothing: the bot posts as itself, to the room its address names.
- The bots page gives each of a bot's rooms its "Slack-compatible webhook URL", with "Copy Slack-compatible webhook URL" beside it.
- Logs filter the key out of the address, as they do the bot API's.

Note: This port's own, so tools that post to Slack can post to a room, as Mattermost, Rocket.Chat, Discord (at `/slack`) and Zulip let them. Emoji names come from emoji-datasource 16.0.0, which `apps/worker/scripts/emoji-names.ts` turns into `src/bots/emoji-names.ts`. Mentions name Slack's ids, which name nobody here. Until cards draw them, attachments and blocks post as rich text. "Slack-compatible" describes the payload: Slack is a trademark of Slack Technologies, LLC, and Ember isn't affiliated with it, as the README says.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Behaviors and sources</summary>

**Send from the keyboard** (`composer.send`) ✅

- On a computer, Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line and Cmd or Ctrl+Enter sends too. With the formatting toolbar open, Enter starts a new line instead, and Enter never sends while an input method is composing.
- On any device with a touchscreen the keyboard never sends, Cmd or Ctrl+Enter included; only the Send button does.
- With the mention list open, Enter picks a mention instead of sending.
- Blank messages aren't sent, though one holding only a mention is. After sending, the toolbar closes and the composer keeps focus, on touch screens too.

Note: Touch is judged by the main pointer, so a laptop with a touchscreen sends on Enter, and Cmd or Ctrl+Enter sends on touch screens too. An address left unfinished in Link, or Link opened out of sight by Cmd or Ctrl+K, doesn't stop Send, where in ember-rust it keeps the message from reaching the server.

Sources: [`crates/assets/overrides/controllers/composer_controller.js`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/assets/overrides/controllers/composer_controller.js) · [`reference/app/javascript/controllers/composer_controller.js`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/app/javascript/controllers/composer_controller.js)

ember-rust tests: [`reference/test/system/composer_test.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/test/system/composer_test.rb) · [`parity/kro/workspace.test.mjs`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/parity/kro/workspace.test.mjs)

**Composer** (`composer.layout`) ✅

- The composer is a rounded card at least 108px tall (100px on phones), with the text on top and Attach files, Formatting options and a round Send button below, on phones too.
- The buttons are titled "Attach files", "Formatting options" and "Send message", and screen readers call them "Attach a file", "Rich text" and "Send Message".
- The text box is named "Write a message", with the placeholder "Message #general" ("Message Ada" in a DM). It grows up to min(32dvh, 300px) and is focused on load, except on touch devices.

Note: Touch is judged by the main pointer, so a laptop with a touchscreen focuses the composer on load. The text takes the card's padding and all the room above the buttons, so a tap anywhere there lands in it: 44px tall on phones, where ember-rust's is 30px. Its text is 16px wherever the main pointer is coarse, as in all of Ember's text fields, so iOS doesn't zoom in on a tablet; ember-rust's is 16px only up to 900px wide. The editor's code, as big as the rest of the app's, loads once the first room's messages are painted, which it would otherwise hold up, so until then the composer shows only its placeholder, and it's focused then only if focus hasn't gone elsewhere meanwhile.

Sources: [`crates/views/templates/rooms/show/_composer.html`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/views/templates/rooms/show/_composer.html) · [`crates/assets/overrides/zz-ember.css`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/assets/overrides/zz-ember.css) · [`crates/assets/overrides/controllers/composer_controller.js`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/assets/overrides/controllers/composer_controller.js)

ember-rust tests: [`parity/kro/workspace.test.mjs`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/parity/kro/workspace.test.mjs) · [`parity/screens.yml`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/parity/screens.yml)

**Keep drafts** (`composer.draft`) ✅

- Whatever you've typed in a room, formatting and mentions included, is kept in this browser (`composer-draft-<room id>`) and restored, cursor at the end, when you come back.
- Sending, or emptying the box, clears it.

Note: Drafts are kept for each person apart (`composer-draft-<user id>-<room id>`), where ember-rust keeps one a room, so whoever signs in on the same browser next doesn't see them.

Sources: [`crates/assets/overrides/controllers/composer_controller.js`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/assets/overrides/controllers/composer_controller.js) · [`reference/app/javascript/controllers/composer_controller.js`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/app/javascript/controllers/composer_controller.js)

**Formatting toolbar** (`composer.formatting-toolbar`) ✅

- Formatting options shows or hides a toolbar under the text: Bold, Italic, Strikethrough, Text formatting (Normal, Large Heading, Clear formatting), Link, Quote, Code, Bullet list and Numbered list. Buttons that don't fit wrap onto another row, and its menus open upward.
- Link, or Cmd or Ctrl+K, asks for an address ("Enter a URL…") with Link and Unlink buttons.
- There's no underline, highlight color, table, divider, undo, redo or upload button, though Cmd or Ctrl+U still underlines.
- Markdown works as you type: `#` headings, `>` quotes, `-`, `*`, `+` and `1.` lists, three backticks for a code block, `---` for a divider, backticks for code, `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `~~strike~~` and `[text](url)`. `==text==` loses its equals signs but keeps no highlight.

Note: This is Lexxy's own toolbar and Markdown, with Campfire's settings and styles, placed and sized as ember-rust's is, and each tool and shortcut writes what ember-rust's does. Two things differ on purpose. Cmd or Ctrl+K shows the toolbar while its Link field is open, where ember-rust opens the field in its hidden toolbar, so nothing seems to happen and the address typed next replaces the selected text. And sending leaves no formatting on, where ember-rust keeps the format the cursor had, so a message sent all in bold leaves the next one bold, with the toolbar that would show it shut.

Sources: [`crates/assets/vendor/lexxy/app/assets/javascript/lexxy.js`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/assets/vendor/lexxy/app/assets/javascript/lexxy.js) · [`reference/app/javascript/initializers/rich_text.js`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/app/javascript/initializers/rich_text.js) · [`reference/app/assets/stylesheets/actiontext.css`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/app/assets/stylesheets/actiontext.css) · [`crates/assets/overrides/zz-ember.css`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/assets/overrides/zz-ember.css) · [`crates/assets/overrides/controllers/composer_controller.js`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/assets/overrides/controllers/composer_controller.js)

ember-rust tests: [`reference/test/system/composer_test.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/test/system/composer_test.rb)

**Pasting into the composer** (`composer.paste`) ✅

- Pasted files join the files waiting to be sent rather than going into the text.
- A pasted address goes in as a link and asks for its preview (see `unfurl.composer`); pasted over selected text, it only turns the selection into a link.
- Pasted text that looks like Markdown is converted, keeping its line breaks; other text goes in as it is, and anything pasted into a code block stays raw.
- Pasted formatting, tables included, is kept as far as messages allow.

Note: Lexxy's own pasting, which writes what ember-rust's does with addresses, Markdown, plain text, code blocks and formatting. Pasted files wait with the files picked to go with the next message (`attachments.upload`).

Sources: [`crates/assets/vendor/lexxy/app/assets/javascript/lexxy.js`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/assets/vendor/lexxy/app/assets/javascript/lexxy.js) · [`crates/assets/overrides/controllers/composer_controller.js`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/assets/overrides/controllers/composer_controller.js)

ember-rust tests: [`reference/test/system/composer_test.rb`](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/blob/90b330024dec3e757c79b6a7e6568f93da8e3148/test/system/composer_test.rb)

<details>
<summary>Behaviors and sources</summary>

**Workspace layout** (`ui.layout`) ✅

- Signed in, the page is the rail (80px), the conversations sidebar (280px, or 230px from 901 to 1100px wide) and the room, under a header at least 60px tall. Text is 14px with a 1.5 line height.
- Light and dark palettes: canvas #fff / #171717, surface #fafafa / #1c1c1c, hover #f2f2f2 / #282828, border #e5e5e5 / #343434, muted #737373 / #a3a3a3, ink #171717 / #f5f5f5.
- Nothing scrolls sideways from 320px to 1440px wide, and the composer stays on screen at 390×420.

Note: The pages few visits need, a room's forms and settings, a DM's settings, the workspace's settings and Custom CSS, the bot pages, your profile and push subscriptions, someone's page and search, load apart from the rest of the app: once the rooms have, while the browser is idle, or at once when the app opens at one of their addresses. One opened before then says Loading… until they have.

Sources: [`crates/views/templates/layouts/application.html`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/views/templates/layouts/application.html) · [`crates/assets/overrides/zz-ember.css`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/assets/overrides/zz-ember.css)

ember-rust tests: [`parity/kro/workspace.test.mjs`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/parity/kro/workspace.test.mjs)

**Rail** (`ui.rail`) ✅

- From the top: the workspace logo (going home, titled with the workspace name), Home, DMs, Activity (a toggle button, `sidebar.activity-filter`), Search, a divider, Admin (Workspace for members), Appearance, and your avatar, a link to your profile named "Your profile" and titled with your name.
- Links are 56px squares with a 22px icon over an 11px label. The current page's link is marked: Home on a room's page (not on a message's permalink), and none while Activity is on.
- DMs opens the new direct message dialog without leaving the page.

Note: Home, Search, Activity and Admin, Workspace for members, work: the logo and Home are marked at home, Home on a room's page, Search on search, Admin or Workspace on workspace settings, your avatar on your profile, and nothing on a room's forms or while Activity is on. DMs opens New direct message over the page (`dms.picker`), which opens at its address, `/rooms/directs/new`, in a new tab. The logo is the workspace's, on the page's background, or Ember's flame while there's none (`accounts.logo`). The links draw Iconoir's icons rather than ember-rust's, as the project's owner chose (`ui.icons`).

**Room header** (`ui.room-header`) ✅

- The header shows the room's icon (`#` by default, the outlined messages icon for DMs) and its name (17px, bold, cut off with …). DM names read as "Direct message with …" to screen readers.
- Rooms have a star to favorite them (`sidebar.favorites`), and on the right Search messages, the notification bell and Conversation settings, which screen readers hear as "Settings for this room", or "Settings for this Ping" in a DM.
- On phones the header is 56px tall and its buttons are 44px squares. Up to 500px wide, the labels of the header's links are hidden too, leaving 44px buttons.

Note: The header has all of ember-rust's: the icon, the name, the star (`sidebar.favorites`), Search messages (`search.page`), the bell (`notifications.levels`) and Conversation settings ("Settings for this room" to screen readers). It also shows who's here (`realtime.who-is-here`), though only to screen readers up to 500px wide, and "Connecting…" or "Reconnecting…" whenever the room's connection isn't open. The star is 44px wide for fingers, where ember-rust's is 32px. Workspace settings' Chat bots and Custom styles show only their icons up to 500px wide, as ember-rust's do, on 44px buttons that keep their names for screen readers.

**Conversations drawer on phones** (`ui.mobile-drawer`) ✅

- At 900px wide and below, the rail and conversations become a drawer opened by the header's 44px Open conversations button, which turns into Close conversations (aria-expanded true) while it's open. It leaves at least 16px of the page showing, and slides in over 180ms unless reduced motion is preferred.
- Opening it dims the page behind, makes the rest of the page inert and focuses its Close conversations button. Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through the rail's and sidebar's controls, and nothing in the drawer can be reached while it's closed.
- Escape, the close button or the backdrop closes it and returns focus to whatever opened it; while a dialog or the appearance menu is open, Escape and Tab are left to them. Following any link in the rail or sidebar closes it, and so does widening the window past 900px.
- Rows and buttons in it are at least 44px tall.

Note: The drawer is a Radix modal dialog named "Conversations", holding the rail and the conversations, where ember-rust slides in the rail and an `aside` that it keeps inert while they're closed, and makes the page behind inert while they're open. Radix hides the page behind from assistive tech, keeps focus in the drawer and takes it off the page while it's closed, which works the same. When a link in it shows another page, focus goes to that page's menu button, where ember-rust's page load leaves nothing focused. A link in it opened somewhere else, such as in a new tab with a modifier key, leaves it open, where ember-rust's shell.js closes it on any click on a rail or sidebar link.

**Light, dark or system appearance** (`ui.appearance`) ✅

- The rail's appearance button, above your avatar, shows a sun, moon or monitor and is named and titled "Appearance: Light", "Appearance: Dark" or "Appearance: System". It opens a small menu, a dialog named Appearance, with Light, Dark and System radio buttons under the legend "Appearance", the current one checked.
- A choice applies at once and leaves the menu open, and the arrow keys move between the choices.
- A choice is kept in this browser (`ember:appearance`, System as `system`) and applied before the page paints, so dark never flashes light. Other open tabs follow, also when the site's storage is cleared or while a tab is still loading, and System follows the device as it changes. Where storage is refused, a choice still holds for the page.
- `<html>` carries the choice in `data-appearance` and the matching `color-scheme`, and once the page is running its theme color follows too, #171717 in dark and #ffffff in light, in place of the starting values (`platform.head-tags`).
- Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the button.

Note: The menu is a Radix popover rather than the browser's Popover API, so it behaves the same in every browser: opening it focuses the current choice, and Tab closes it and goes on from the button, as ember-rust's menu does where the browser lacks the Popover API. With the API, ember-rust leaves focus on the button as the menu opens and leaves the menu open as focus moves on. The button only exists once the app runs, so there's nothing to keep hidden until then. Every page follows other tabs and the device, setup included, and recolors the browser around it, where ember-rust's setup pages keep the system's theme colors. The `matchbox:appearance` and `campfire:appearance` keys earlier versions saved aren't read, since no browser has them for this app (`platform.rename-compat`). The button and the menu show Iconoir's Sun Light, Half Moon and Computer rather than Lucide's sun, moon and monitor, as the rail's links draw Iconoir's icons (`ui.icons`).

**Stay at the newest message** (`ui.scroll`) ✅

- Rooms open at the newest message. A new message scrolls into view only if you were within 100px of the bottom; otherwise, or whenever one arrives while you're reading older history, a centered Jump to newest message button appears. It hides once the newest message comes into view.
- Clicking it, or sending, scrolls to the bottom, loading the newest messages first if you were reading history.
- An edit or a new reaction keeps your place.
- Past 320 messages the page is cut back to 300, dropping the end you're furthest from; scrolling back to a cut end loads it again.

Note: The button is ember-rust's, measured against its own, except that it's 44px on touch screens, as Ember's controls are, and it hides once you're back within 100px of the newest message. New messages that arrive while you're reading older history wait until you go to the newest, where ember-rust adds them below the history it has loaded, past the messages it hasn't.

**Empty room** (`ui.empty-room`) ✅

- A room nobody has written in says "Welcome to #&lt;room&gt;" and "This is the very beginning of the room. Say hello!"
- The workspace's first room shows the welcome card instead, while it has one (`rooms.invitation-card`).

**Select a field's text on entry** (`ui.select-on-entry`) ✅

- Tabbing or clicking into a text, search, email, URL, phone or password field selects what's in it, so typing replaces it. A second click, or a drag, places the cursor as usual.
- Text areas and the message box are never selected, nor are disabled or read-only fields and three marked ones: the workspace name, direct-message search and icon search.
- It works on every page but first-run setup, signed in or not.

Note: Ported from shell.js, listening from the moment the app opens, so a field focused as its page opens is selected too, as New room's name is. ember-rust's mark, `data-ember-preserve-selection`, keeps the usual cursor; Set up Ember carries it on its page, for all its fields, and Workspace name on its field. New direct message's search carries it too. Two things differ from ember-rust. A press selects when its click comes, not as it focuses the field: pressing on selected text drags it, so in ember-rust a drag across a field that isn't focused picks up all its text instead of selecting part of it. And coming back to the window leaves the field you were in as it was: browsers focus it again then, which ember-rust takes for entering it, so carrying on typing there replaces what was typed before.

**Saved notices** (`ui.flash`) ✅

- A notice shows as a toast below the header, centered over the content (over the whole window when signed out, or at 900px wide and below): a check and the text, in white on green. An alert is red, with an alert sign.
- It fades in after 0.3 seconds and fades out again, leaving the page 3.3 seconds after it loaded. Screen readers hear it as an alert, and a notice of just "✓" shows only the check, read as "Changes saved".
- Saving the workspace's name or logo says "Changes saved.", saving custom styles or your profile "✓", and a new profile photo "It may take up to 30 minutes to change everywhere." The settings switches, which save as you flip them, show none.
- Opening a room that's gone or isn't yours goes home with the alert "Room not found or inaccessible", and a refused sign-in shows "Too many requests or unauthorized."

Note: Notices and alerts show one at a time, over any page, and a page that loads another in its place can leave one for it, as ember-rust's redirects carry theirs. Saving the workspace's name or logo says "Changes saved.", saving custom styles or your profile "✓", and a new profile photo "It may take up to 30 minutes to change everywhere." The alerts are a refused sign-in's, "Room not found or inaccessible" from a room or its settings, and why creating or saving a room, or saving the workspace's name or your profile, failed ("Couldn't reach Ember. Check your connection and try again." when the server can't be reached). Unlike ember-rust's, it shows under reduced motion, at once and without fading, until the fade would have ended, where Campfire's reset cuts the animation to nothing so ember-rust's never shows; it grows to fit its text, up to the window's width less 24px, where ember-rust's stops at half the window's width and wraps early on a phone; and it keeps 12px below the header, and centered over the page, where they make room for a notch.

**Landmarks and names** (`ui.accessibility`) ✅

- Skip to main content is the first thing Tab reaches. It's hidden until focused, and moves focus to the main content.
- Landmarks are named: navigation "Workspace" (the rail) and "Page" (the header), "Conversations" (the sidebar) with Rooms and DMs, and the main content.
- Controls without visible text have names: the message box "Write a message", "Attach a file", "Rich text", "Send Message", "Jump to newest message", "Open conversations" or "Close conversations", and "Your profile".
- The current room and rail link are marked `aria-current="page"`, toggles such as Activity and the star are `aria-pressed`, focus shows a 2px outline, and status changes and errors are announced.

Note: The skip link and the landmarks are ember-rust's, though following the skip link leaves the address as it is, where ember-rust's adds `#main-content`, and the first-run page has them too, as ember-rust's basecoat layout does. The message log ("Messages in general") and the composer are named, and so are the icon-only buttons, as in ember-rust: "Write a message", "Attach a file", "Rich text", "Send Message", "Jump to newest message", Activity and the star, which say whether they're on.

<details>
<summary>Behaviors and sources</summary>

**Health check** (`platform.health`) ✅

- `GET /up` answers 200 with exactly `<!DOCTYPE html><html><body style="background-color: green"></body></html>` as `text/html; charset=utf-8`. `/up.json`, or `/up` with `Accept: application/json`, answers `{"status":"up","timestamp":…}` with the time to the second.
- It skips sign-in, ban and browser checks, and carries no version headers.

Note: `/up` picks its format as Rails does: from the extension, else from an Accept header that isn't a browser's, with `Vary: Accept`, and 406 for any other format. Beside it, `GET /api/health` goes deeper: it answers 200 only once `SESSION_SECRET` is set and the Workspace and a room's object have both read their storage, and 503 otherwise, logging why. Strangers hear `{ ok }` alone, so a deployment doesn't describe itself to them; an administrator, or a request carrying `EMBER_RECOVERY_TOKEN` as its bearer token, hears `{ ok: true, storage, push, files }`, which says whether push notifications are on and an R2 bucket for files is bound, or `{ ok: false, storage, error }`. It isn't checked for old browsers either, and the deploy check relies on it instead of signing in, hearing the storage when it has the token.

Sources: [`crates/ember/src/controllers.rs`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/ember/src/controllers.rs)

ember-rust tests: [`crates/ember/src/app/tests.rs`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/ember/src/app/tests.rs)

**Error pages** (`platform.error-pages`) ✅

- A missing page answers 404, a write refused as cross-site 422 and a server failure 500, each with a standalone page titled "We can’t find that (404)", "That didn’t work (422)" or "Something went wrong (500)": an illustration and a Go back button to `/`, plus Try again, which reloads, on the 422 page.
- A request for JSON gets `{"status":404,"error":"Not Found"}` instead, with the matching status and reason.
- The 502 page says "Starting Ember…" with the logo and reloads itself every 10 seconds.
- `/robots.txt` is served, and allows everything.

Note: The Worker serves the app's page only at the addresses the app shows a page at, which `@ember/protocol` lists for the app's router too; the built app answers any other path with one of its files or Campfire's 404 page (`not_found_handling`), and the Worker answers a write to a page, an unknown address under `/first_run` and a QR code's address without a code with the 404 page itself. Rails' unused actions, such as `/rooms/new`, are 404s as in ember-rust, but My profile, New direct message and a DM's settings, which the app links to before it has them, go home for now. Where ember-rust ignores a trailing or doubled slash, the Worker redirects to the page's own address, which the app reads. No page takes a write, so only the API sees a cross-site one, and it refuses it with JSON, as it answers every error, an exception's included (`{ "error": "Something went wrong" }`), where ember-rust answers any JSON request with `{"status":…,"error":…}`; elsewhere a JSON request gets the page. On setup's form, an exception's log says only that the request failed, as ember-rust's does. Campfire's pages have no viewport, so a phone shrinks them to fit a 980px layout and Go back is too small to tap; these add one, and a language. An old browser gets the upgrade page even at an unknown address, since that check comes first (`platform.browser-support`). There's no 502 page: a Worker has no start-up to wait through, and a deploy switches over at once. Each of the app's pages comes with a Link header that has the browser fetch what the app asks for first along with the page: `/api/bootstrap`, and on a page with the sidebar, for a browser with a session cookie, `/api/sidebar` and `/api/users`; so the page varies with the cookie. Campfire's 422 page reloads with an inline onclick on Try again, which Ember's policy (`platform.security-headers`) refuses, so Ember's has an empty href, which loads the same address again.

**Durable Object SQLite or D1** (`platform.storage`) ✅

- Messages and boosts live in each room's Durable Object SQLite by default, or in D1 when `STORAGE_BACKEND` is `d1`, and behave the same either way.
- Wrangler applies every file in `apps/worker/migrations/` to D1. On DO SQLite, each Durable Object applies the files for its own kind of object (`MIGRATIONS` names each file's scope) that it's missing when it opens, recording each so it runs once, so a room never holds another kind's tables.
- A write that has to be atomic is one batch: on either backend its statements run in order and all take effect, or, if one fails, none do.

**Hibernating rooms** (`platform.hibernation`) ✅

- Room Durable Objects hibernate between messages without dropping sockets: who's connected survives a wake-up, and pings are answered without waking the room.

**One live connection per tab outside the open room** (`platform.live-socket`) ✅

- Each signed-in tab keeps one socket besides the room's. It carries unread and read marks, DM activity, sidebar and star changes, and requests to reload the sidebar, for every room the person is in.
- It reconnects with the room socket's back-off and heartbeat, and the sidebar is fetched again once it's back.
- Nobody hears about a room they aren't in, and an event reaches only the members whose sidebar it changes.
- Signing out or losing access to a room closes it as `realtime.connection` describes, and nothing more about a room you've left reaches you.

Note: Each signed-in tab opens `/api/socket` to the Workspace Durable Object, which lets it in with a welcome naming who the session signs in, answers its pings, and closes the session's sockets, saying to reconnect, when it signs out. It reconnects with the room socket's back-off and heartbeat, and the sidebar loads again each time it connects. It also tells each person when a room is marked unread or read for them (`sidebar.unread`). It also brings DM activity (`sidebar.dm-order`), rooms saved, made, changed or gone (`sidebar.live-updates`), stars (`sidebar.favorites`), rooms hidden or shown (`notifications.hide-room`), and the shared order, which has the sidebar load again (`sidebar.shared-order`).

**Version** (`platform.version`) ✅

- Pages and the app's other responses carry X-Version: `APP_VERSION` if set, else `GIT_REVISION`, else the release ("1.1", the package version without a trailing ".0"); blank values count as unset. X-Rev carries `GIT_REVISION` whenever it's set, even blank.
- `/up`, static files and the live connection carry neither header.
- Workspace settings show "Ember™ version &lt;same value&gt;" at the bottom, and so do the sign-in and join pages under the help contact, when there's an administrator to contact.

**Supported browsers** (`platform.browser-support`) ✅

- Safari before 17.2, Chrome before 120, Firefox before 121, Opera before 104, and Internet Explorer get "Upgrade to a supported web browser" with status 200, whatever was asked for, the manifest and JSON requests included. Signed out, it shows in place of the sign-in page.
- Chromium Edge, Chrome on iOS and Samsung Internet count as Chrome, by their Chrome version; Firefox on iOS counts as Safari at the iOS version, and Edge on iOS by its Safari version.
- Legacy Edge, other browsers, bots, user agents without a version and requests without a user agent get through, and `/up` is never checked.
- The page is titled "Unsupported browser" ("Ember" for Apple Messages' link previews), says "Ember requires a modern web browser. Please use one of the browsers listed below and make sure auto-updates are enabled." and lists Safari 17.2+, Chrome 120+, Firefox 121+ and Opera 104+ with their icons.

Note: Every user agent in ember-rust's vectors gets its verdict. Where ember-rust's reading parts from Rails', this follows Rails: an agent calling itself "IE" is turned away, and a "MicroMeßenger" is WeChat, as Ruby folds case. An agent Rails fails to read, which Campfire answers with an error page, gets through. The Worker writes the page itself in plain CSS, since the app's stylesheet needs a supported browser, and always with the signed-out layout, where ember-rust puts a signed-in person's rail around it: nothing past the page runs in that browser. It checks before anything but `/up` and `/api/health`, where ember-rust checks after sign-in and its forgery check, so a signed-out request for the API gets the page rather than 401. The logos are Campfire's, served from `/browsers/`. Its translation globe shows once an administrator shows translation buttons (`accounts.translation-buttons`), as ember-rust's does, and Campfire's globe.svg is served as the logos are.

**Security headers and HTTPS** (`platform.security-headers`) ✅

- Pages and other responses the app renders (not static files, streamed files or error pages) carry `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, `X-XSS-Protection: 0`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies: none` and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.
- Unless `DISABLE_SSL` is set, plain HTTP redirects to the same URL over HTTPS, every HTTPS response carries `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains`, and every cookie is `Secure`.
- Everything the Worker answers but a room's files carries a `Content-Security-Policy`, Ember's own: scripts from this origin and a page's own inline scripts by hash; styles from this origin or inline; images from this origin, any HTTPS host, data and blob URLs; media from this origin and blob URLs; connections and sockets to this host; no plugins; frames, forms and base URLs only to this origin; and violations reported to `/csp-report`, which the Worker logs.

Note: Page loads go through the Worker (`run_worker_first`, all but the built app's static files), which adds Rails' headers to everything it answers, its errors included, where ember-rust's error pages go without; a room socket's upgrade gets none. Plain HTTP gets ember-rust's TLS front's answer: 301 to the same address over HTTPS for every method, with a link for a GET. ember-rust's also keeps setup's addresses out of caches and referrers and refuses them with a query, which could hold its setup token; Ember's token rides in the fragment, which no request carries (`auth.protected-setup`), so they're redirected like any other. HSTS goes on every HTTPS answer from the Worker, but static files go without it. Localhost and loopback addresses are never redirected and get no HSTS, so `wrangler dev` works as it is and HSTS never sticks to them; `DISABLE_SSL` turns both off anywhere else. Cookies are `Secure` whenever the request is HTTPS, which away from loopback it always is unless `DISABLE_SSL` is set. The policy is Ember's, which Campfire and ember-rust go without, as the backstop should markup get past the sanitizer, Lexxy or a dependency. The app's page names its theme script by hash, read from the built page once per deploy, and the upgrade page names its two; `style-src` allows inline styles, which React's style attributes, Lexxy and custom CSS need, and `img-src https:` lets previews show their page's image. A room's files go without a policy: nothing served from `/files/` can run script, and Chrome's PDF viewer is particular about one. `connect-src` names the host for sockets, since Safari reads `'self'` as the page's scheme alone.

**Deploy secrets** (`platform.deploy-secrets`) ✅

- A deploy without `SESSION_SECRET` generates one, and later deploys keep it; a failed lookup of the Worker's secrets stops the deploy rather than replacing one.
- A deploy without either VAPID key generates a pair, and later deploys keep it, so browsers' push subscriptions outlast deploys; a Worker with just one key keeps it.
- Secrets go live with the code in a single deploy, and none appears in logs or the run summary.
- The installer prints the private setup link, `https://<host>/first_run/access#token=<token>`, once the server is up, and `emberctl setup-link` prints it again.
- The deploy check says whether Ember is set up yet.

Note: `pnpm run deploy` (`apps/worker/scripts/deploy.ts`) makes the secrets a Worker is missing and uploads them with the code through `wrangler deploy --secrets-file`, for Deploy to Cloudflare's builds, which ask the deployer for none, and the Preview workflow alike. Cloudflare's build logs mask nothing, so the script never prints a secret, except the one meant to be read: a Worker without `EMBER_SETUP_TOKEN` gets one, and once wrangler has deployed, the script prints the setup link that carries it (`auth.protected-setup`), `https://<the Worker>/first_run#token=<token>`, from the address wrangler records of the deploy. A CI log can be public, as a public repository's Actions logs are, so under `CI` the script makes no token and says so (as a `::notice::` under GitHub Actions), unless `EMBER_SETUP_TOKEN` in its environment brings one, which it uploads and leaves out of the log, printing the link's shape instead; Workers Builds (`WORKERS_CI`) is the account's own log, so Deploy to Cloudflare gets its link there. The Preview workflow passes an `EMBER_SETUP_TOKEN` repository secret through, if there is one. There's no `setup-link` command: the token is a Worker secret, which `wrangler secret put EMBER_SETUP_TOKEN` replaces when the link is lost, and the deploy's hint names the Worker deployed (`--name`, `--config`) so a new token goes to it rather than wrangler.jsonc's. The deploy check says whether setup waits for the link, is open, or can't happen for want of a token.

Sources: [`deploy/installer/emberctl.py`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/deploy/installer/emberctl.py) · [`crates/ember/src/admin.rs`](https://github.com/NYLLON-SOFTWARE/ember-rust/blob/cfeb4c289f9ab3042248777f29a103294ff3de87/crates/ember/src/admin.rs)
